facts.text: Stockton was first called Lancaster, then renamed Fremont in 1847 after John C. Fremont, and finally took its current name in 1857 honoring Robert F. Stockton.
The Stockton Community Building, a centerpiece of downtown, earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places.
Stockton sits just west of the Stockton Lake dam, about 40 miles northwest of Springfield, offering scenic river views.
The city’s workforce spans banks, retailers, factories, schools, offices, general services, and self‑employment, reflecting a diverse local economy.
In fall 2011, Stockton upgraded its sewer system with 17,630 linear feet of clay tile, rehabilitated 60 manholes, and reconnected 110 lateral lines to support future growth.
The old wastewater lagoon system failed to meet quality standards after the 2003 tornado, prompting upgrades to avoid effluent limit violations.
